hooks.text: Sunlight and neutrinos born together escape the Sun thousands of years apart.
Sunlight warming your skin took thousands of years to escape the core.
Why does sunlight take thousands of years to escape its own star?

title: The Sunlight Warming Your Face Is Prehistoric
description: While neutrinos flee the Sun's core in two seconds, radiant light takes tens of thousands of years to escape. The Borexino experiment proved our Sun's core produces the same energy today as it did during the Ice Age.

beats.text: Sunlight and neutrinos born together escape the Sun thousands of years apart.
beats.visual: Solar Dynamics Observatory extreme ultraviolet view of the Sun, 2015
queries: SDO atmospheric imaging assembly full disk
Solar Dynamics Observatory extreme ultraviolet Sun

beats.text: Deep inside the Sun's core, nuclear fusion converts hydrogen protons into helium, unleashing radiant energy alongside neutrinos.
beats.visual: Illustration of the Sun's interior layers showing core and radiative zone
queries: Sun interior diagram core radiative zone

beats.text: Because neutrinos interact extremely weakly with matter, they shoot through the dense interior and reach the surface in approximately two seconds.
beats.visual: Diagram of proton-proton fusion chain creating neutrinos and energy

beats.text: Light energy faces an endless maze. Trapped in the crushing interior, that energy repeatedly scatters, absorbs, and re-emits.
beats.visual: Diagram showing photon scattering and random walk in solar radiative zone

beats.text: That sluggish journey traps the energy for thousands to hundreds of thousands of years before it finally escapes.
beats.visual: Solar Dynamics Observatory full disk image of solar surface granulation, 2019

beats.text: By detecting both signals, the [Borexino](/bˈOɹˈɛksˈinˈO/) experiment proved the Sun releases the same amount of energy today as it did 100,000 years ago.
beats.visual: Photograph of the Borexino neutrino detector sphere inside Gran Sasso, 2014

beats.text: While neutrinos deliver live updates from the core, the light warming your skin is an ancient relic.
beats.visual: High-resolution view of sunlight bursting from the Sun's limb, SDO, 2021

better_than_last: Replaced technical acronyms and academic debates in middle beats with an immediate physical comparison between neutrino and light timescales to sustain narrative tension.
